lastUpdatedBy.description: Last actor who updated the content, derived from history (or author fallback). Null when neither history nor author resolves.

email.description: Email from the user view when available.

reference.description: External reference (e.g. HR id) when stored on the user view.

primaryCategory.description: The content type category of this content. `standard` is the category the platform displays as "Mixed". Present when a record is read by its id or returned by a v2 write, for content held by the content source that carries the category; `null` when such a record predates the category and none was set since. The field is not present in the results of the list endpoint, nor on a record that exists only in the legacy content source ,  its `type` already holds the display value there. The API sets. See the official API reference for further details.

provider.description: The content provider. Defaults to Thrive for natively created content.

signedPutUrls.description: One entry for each upload item added, and each item whose file was replaced, in this request, plus one for the thumbnail when the request carried `thumbnail`. Empty when the request carried none of them. In the rare case that the thumbnail URL could not be issued after an update, its entry is missing while the update was still applied; send a `PATCH` with `thumbnail` to get one. A request that carries only `thumbnail` applies no update, so it answers an error instead when the URL cannot be issued.

items.description: A presigned URL to `PUT` one upload's bytes to: an item file, or the content thumbnail image.

skills.description: The `tags` entries that the taxonomy marks as a skill. Additive: every name is also in `tags`. A tag the taxonomy does not hold is in neither `skills` nor `topics`. Both fields are absent when the taxonomy cannot be read.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the content. A legacy (content-service) record derives the value: archived content reports `archived`, content with a publish time reports `published`, and all other content reports `created`. A content-core record maps its lifecycle status onto the same values, where draft and ready both report `created`. `deleted` is a filter value only and is never returned: a legacy record returned by a `deleted` status filter reports its pre-deletion state, and a deleted content-core record is physically gone.

tags.description: List of tags associated with this content. Omitted when the tag source cannot be read, so an absent field means "tags unavailable" rather than "no tags".

topics.description: The `tags` entries that the taxonomy marks as a topic. Additive: every name is also in `tags`. A tag the taxonomy does not hold is in neither `topics` nor `skills`. Both fields are absent when the taxonomy cannot be read.

type.description:
The kind of artifact associated with this content record.

Courses are represented as `pathway`. Pathways will be served by a dedicated Pathways API in a future release and will stop appearing on this endpoint at that point, so treat `pathway` as temporary here.

updatedAt.description: Timestamp when the content was last updated

anyOf.description: Served when the content was created or updated but could not be read back. The write was applied ,  do not retry. Fetch the full record with `GET /contents/{id}`.

signedPutUrls.description: On a create, one entry for each upload item in the request. On an update, one entry for each upload item added and each item whose file was replaced. Plus one for the thumbnail when the request carried `thumbnail`. Empty when the request carried none.

items.description: A presigned URL to `PUT` one upload's bytes to: an item file, or the content thumbnail image.

data.description: The updated content with its presigned upload URLs. In the rare case that the content was updated but could not be read back, the response is the minimal form: `id`, `status` and `signedPutUrls` only. The update was applied in both cases ,  do not retry the request. A full body also satisfies the minimal shape, so this is `anyOf`.
